original_value: Closing feedback loops fast and over long distances is key to emerging cyber-physical applications; for example, robot motion control and swarm coordination require update intervals of tens of milliseconds. Low-power wireless communication technology is preferred for its low cost, small form factor, and flexibility, especially if the devices support multi-hop communication. Thus far, however, feedback control over multi-hop low-power wireless networks has only been demonstrated for update intervals on the order of seconds. To fill this gap, this article presents a wireless embedded system that supports dynamic mode changes and tames imperfections impairing control performance (e.g., jitter and message loss), and a control design that exploits the essential properties of this system to provably guarantee closed-loop stability for physical processes with linear time-invariant dynamics in the presence of mode changes. Using experiments on a cyber-physical testbed with 20 wireless devices and multiple cart-pole systems, we are the first to demonstrate and evaluate feedback control and coordination with mode changes over multi-hop networks for update intervals of 20 to 50 milliseconds.

result.paraphrase: Rapid feedback over both short and long distances is essential for emerging cyber-physical applications; for instance, robot motion control and swarm coordination need update intervals measured in tens of milliseconds. Low-power wireless communication is favored because it is inexpensive, compact, and flexible, particularly when devices can communicate over multiple hops. So far, though, feedback control across multi-hop low-power wireless networks has only been shown at update intervals on the order of seconds. To address this gap, the article introduces a wireless embedded system with dynamic mode switching that mitigates imperfections that degrade control performance, such as jitter and message loss, together with a control strategy that leverages the system’s key properties to provably ensure closed-loop stability for physical processes with linear time-invariant dynamics despite mode changes. Experiments on a cyber-physical testbed with 20 wireless devices and multiple cart-pole systems make us the first to demonstrate and assess feedback control and coordination with mode changes over multi-hop networks at update intervals of 20 to 50 milliseconds.
